idiom_name: plain mapping function between parsed JSON shapes (JSON.parse / JSON.stringify)
implementation_notes: In JavaScript the translator is an ordinary function: JSON.parse yields a plain object, the mapping is destructuring plus an object literal, and JSON.stringify re-emits it, so the adapter half of the classic pattern collapses into the function's parameter and return shape (MDN JSON). There is no annotation or reflection layer to configure, so the explicit function is the idiomatic form; when the wire contract is IDL-owned, generated codecs (protobuf.js, Avro) replace it, and a Translator object is only worth writing when the mapping needs a registry of versions or injected lookups.
pitfalls: JSON round-trips silently lose precision on 64-bit integers above 2^53 and turn Date objects into ISO strings, so a translated id or timestamp can change value across the hop.
Mapping untrusted input with Object.assign/merge spreads prototype-pollution keys (__proto__, constructor) into the target; whitelist the fields you copy.
undefined differs from missing: JSON.stringify drops undefined properties, so downstream code checking `key in obj` versus `!== undefined` behaves differently after a translation hop.
